audited_plan.image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on blue water. The bird is facing left, displaying a clear profile of its iridescent green head, white neck ring, and yellow-green bill with a black tip. The body features brownish-grey plumage, and the characteristic curled tail feathers are visible at the rear.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible in profile. It exhibits the correct broad, flat shape and the characteristic color gradient from yellow-green at the base to a black tip. The edge definition against the neck is distinct.
A dark eye is clearly visible on the side of the green head, positioned correctly relative to the bill.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a floating duck—streamlined, low in the water, and appearing buoyant with tight feather texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged underwater and not visible in this floating pose.
The folded wings are visible along the flank, appearing broad and tapering towards the tail, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (sex feathers) is clearly visible at the rear of the duck.

artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a slight softness and lack of distinct feather definition where the green head meets the white neck ring and the brown chest. The transition looks slightly painted or smoothed rather than having crisp individual feather boundaries, which is a common AI artifact in high-contrast plumage areas.

While the bill is visible, the junction where the bill meets the throat feathers shows minor ambiguity. The hard edge of the beak softens slightly into the feathers, suggesting a very subtle rendering imperfection, though not a catastrophic failure.

Verify that the water displacement around the chest looks physically accurate for an object of this mass.
